Three supplies, one star point — sheet 2 of 3. Signals on SCHEMA_SIGNALS.svg, wiring on SCHEMA_WIRING.svg
Independent supplies are fine. What is NOT optional is that every negative meets at one point — that is the only thing that makes the links work.

STAR GROUND — EVERY NEGATIVE MEETS HERE
Three supplies, one reference. Miss this and the UART links and I²C have no common zero — which looks exactly like a firmware bug.
What an Arduino 3.3 V pin gives
Even the average exceeds a CH340 board's
3.3 V pin. This is not marginal — the ESP32
would brown out and reset in a loop, and you
would be cooking the Arduino's regulator.
LOGIC → 9 V. The MCX takes it through a
buck module to 5 V at J3-10 — its own VIN
pin is not wired to work. The ESP32 takes
the same 9 V on VIN, with a fan on its regulator.
Do NOT use a PP3 block: ~500 mAh, and it sags
TRACTION → either works now. The MG90S
4.8–6.0 V window was what used to force NiMH
here; with the servos gone the TT motors are
happy on 4.8 V or 6 V alike.
NiMH is still the better choice: it holds its
voltage under a stall where alkalines sag.
Label the two packs. They are not swappable.
WHAT THE MCX PACK COSTS YOU
Running the MCX from a pack instead of
MCU-Link USB means no VCOM: no console,
During development, keep the USB cable in
and leave the pack off. Check UM12012 for
the power-select jumper before feeding both
The pack is for the untethered demo run.
The ESP32 still needs it then, so wire the
pack now and just leave it switched off.
Nothing else changes: logic levels do not
depend on which supply feeds a board, so
both 1 kΩ / 2 kΩ dividers stay exactly as
1. Every negative meets at the star point: traction pack −, logic pack −, USB ground,
all four board grounds, all four transistor emitters, every component GND.
2. Feed the ESP32 at VIN, never at the 3V3 pin. Its on-board regulator does the rest,
and it wants a 470 µF nearby to absorb the WiFi transmit bursts.
3. Never feed pack voltage into an Arduino 5 V pin, or 6 V into the MCX 3.3 V rail.
4. Power up together, or logic pack first. A powered Arduino driving an unpowered MCX
pushes current through its ESD diodes — the 1 kΩ divider resistor limits it to a
harmless few mA, which is a second reason those dividers are not optional.
5. The MAX7219 at full brightness pulls 300 mA from PERC's USB. Keep intensity low.
6. Motor and servo current never touches an Arduino or the MCX. Only signals and ground.
SUPPLY WINDOWS — WHAT VIN CAN BE, PER BOARD

The 9 V logic pack feeds the MCX and the ESP32 directly. It does NOT suit the Arduinos — their regulator's dropout, so their 5 V rail would sag to about 4.7 V.
If you ever want the Arduinos off a pack too, that pack has to be 7.2 V (6 × NiMH) or 9 V — or feed their 5V pins from something already regulated to 5 V.
